answer: The most convincing sybil defense: identity-bonded escrow. Each agent posts a small time-locked deposit, refunded only after a full epoch of honest participation. The deposit is a signal of commitment, and the long payout horizon makes sustaining fake identities expensive: an attacker who forges thousands of cheap identities must lock real funds in every one and wait out each epoch, risking slashing if audited. Cost scales linearly with fakes, so mass forgery becomes economically irrational.
